skills.title: Cards, legal actions and additional payment
criteria: Construct exactly five available cards; distinguish private cards from the shared board.
Uses six cards, requires both private cards, or names a card that is unavailable.
Count an additional call as the current wager minus this round's contribution.
Subtracts an earlier round's payment or adds an already posted blind twice.
Explain when checking, betting, calling, folding or a legal raise is available under the stated assumptions.
Checks past an unmatched bet or treats every contribution as a new raise.
skills.probe: If the learner says the right number but subtracts preflop chips from a flop call, would the feedback expose that reason?

skills.title: Position and players still to act
criteria: Follow the six-player initial preflop order through button, small blind and big blind.
Says the button ends preflop or counts posting a blind as taking an initial turn.
Rebuild postflop order from remaining seats clockwise after the button.
Carries preflop order into the flop or moves blinds after other players fold.
Explain how earlier action, price and relevant stacks change a situation with the same two cards.
Uses a hand label or seat alone to prescribe an action without those facts.
skills.probe: Can the text distinguish two players remaining from a hand originally dealt heads-up? The examples remain six-player deals.

skills.title: Made hand, draw and observed action
criteria: Name the current best five and count the suit cards actually available.
Calls four suited cards a completed flush or overlooks a made pair beside a draw.
Explain that improving and winning are different claims.
Treats a completed draw as a guaranteed win regardless of later board or opposing cards.
Read a check or bet as an action and explain the resulting options.
Treats a check as proof of weakness or allows checking again past a new bet.
skills.probe: Would a confident answer of 'a flush' be repaired by counting the exact hearts or spades rather than only revealing the category?

skills.title: Rebuild the hand and distinguish price from equity
criteria: Rebuild the best five after the turn and river, including changed kickers and missed draws.
Keeps an obsolete kicker, waits for a card after the river or awards the wrong showdown winner.
For the stated final heads-up call, divide the additional call by the pot after calling.
Omits the caller's extra chips from the denominator or treats the bet size alone as the price.
State the no-fee, no-side-pot, no-prize-effect assumptions and distinguish required pot share, including ties, from estimated equity.
Treats 20% or 25% as a measured winning probability or an automatic instruction to call.
skills.probe: Can the reviewer derive e(P+C)-C = 0 and explain why that prices this call without ranking every available action?

skills.title: Known cards, possible holdings and frequencies
criteria: Remove candidates that reuse a known exact card and compare each remaining candidate separately.
Allows a duplicate card or combines mutually exclusive candidates into one physical deal.
Compare legal candidates with the hero's best five without assigning unsupported frequencies.
Makes all listed candidates equally likely or calls a small candidate list a complete range.
Separate a check or one showdown reveal from an estimate of how often a holding takes that action.
Uses one revealed hand or a checked turn to establish or eliminate an entire frequency model.
skills.probe: If two possible models allow the same observed hand, does the explanation keep both possible until more evidence is supplied?

skills.title: Bet purpose, alternatives and outcome bias
criteria: Identify worse callers for a value argument and better folders for a bluff argument.
Calls any winning bet value or any losing hand a profitable bluff.
Compare betting with checking using frequencies, amounts, other responses and future action where relevant.
Treats naming one worse caller or holding a strong category as a complete betting verdict.
Keep the scripted result separate from the quality of the earlier decision.
Uses a win or loss as proof of the best action or implies profitable-play readiness from this course.
skills.probe: Can the restricted response assumptions support the stated comparison without pretending to describe an actual player's measured range?
